$comment: The harness catalog. The frontend-harness skill reads it to suggest modules; tasks/apply.mjs reads it to install them. Each module is one thing the project gets; `dependencies` lists everything it needs by name: other `modules`, `plugins` (plugins.json), `skills` (skills.json), `mcp` servers (mcp.json), `rules` (rules.json), `configs` (configs.json: configs and other project files), `hooks` (hooks.json), `githooks` (githooks.json), `permissions` (permissions.json), and npm `devDependencies` (and `frameworkDevDependencies`). Each of those catalogs says how its entries get into the project: `install` or `input`, with `output` and `mode`. A `group` takes exactly `pick` of its modules; `default` names the one to use per framework when the project shows none.

linter.description: The linter the hooks and checks run.

core.description: Claude Code hooks, the structure rule, typecheck and Prettier on every edit and turn.

format:file.description: Prettier on one file (used by the edit hook)

check.description: all checks at once, as the Stop hook runs them

prepare.description: turns on the git hooks in .githooks/ (npm runs it on install)

sections.Several agents at once:
- Several agents may work in this repo at the same time, all on `main`. Changes you did not make are another agent's work in progress, not a mess to clean up.
- Touch only your own changes. Never revert, reformat, stash or commit another agent's files.
- Before editing a file, check `git status`. If it has changes you did not make, tell the user which file and wait instead of editing it.
- If the end-of-turn checks fail, first make sure none of the failures come from your own changes. If they all sit in another agent's files, finish with one short line saying so; do not analyse, list or fix them.
- Commit only your own files (`git add <paths>`, never `git add -A`).

unit.description: Vitest unit tests, run at the end of every turn.

e2e.description: Playwright end-to-end tests, the playwright-cli skill for browser checks, and a pre-push hook that runs them.

verify.description: all end-to-end tests; `npx playwright test <file>` for one

commitlint.description: Conventional Commits checked by commitlint in a commit-msg hook, plus the skill that writes valid messages.

quality.description: knip (unused files, exports, dependencies) and jscpd (duplicated code), run at the end of every turn.

best-practices.description: Best-practice skills for the framework: Vercel's React and Next.js performance rules, composition patterns and the Web Interface Guidelines review.

context7.description: Context7 MCP server, rule and skill for current library docs.
